content:
oncall-bot Incident created: alert=prod-gpu-container-oom, severity=high, region=us-west-2, cluster=prod-kv, node=prod-kv-08

oncall-bot Note: automated log snapshot attached.

sam.h saw this: Prometheus firing 3472005677. Multiple containers on prod-kv-08 crashed with CUDA OOM and then node started flapping.
anya.p I see the same in logs. KV paged allocator showing steady resident set creep over 18h, then spike. Likely fragmentation + slow leak, hits OOM at ~90% allocation.

david.r Can someone confirm customer impact? Any 5xx spikes?
ml-infra Checking traces: a small subset of requests hitting long-context whisper models routed through paged KV path. Error rate up ~3.4% in US-W, latency tail up. Affected customers: two midmarket tenants with high batch loads.

sre-lead ok triage plan: 1) contain blast radius 2) restart affected containers 3) apply mitigation to allocator config 4) collect full heap maps for postmortem. Who takes node?

sam.h I'll take node prod-kv-08. Repeating steps: drain new requests to other nodes, restart runtime on that host.
anya.p Steps I recommend before restart: disable attention paging on that host so allocator uses resident-only path. Env toggle: ATTENTION_PAGING=0 (will increase memory but should avoid fragmentation path).
ml-infra Command I ran to check fragmentation metrics:

```
curl -s http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=kvcache_fragmentation_ratio
# sample output:
# {instance=\"prod-kv-08\", job=\"kv-allocator\"} 0.78
```

sam.h doing drain: `kubectl cordon prod-kv-08` then `kubectl drain prod-kv-08 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

oncall-bot Automated: cordon+drain initiated by sam.h at 3472005690.

sam.h Restarting runtime container on prod-kv-08 now. Command: `docker restart redwood-runtime`

(10s later)
sam.h runtime restarted, container came back but OOMs resumed after ~2 minutes. CUDA error shows kernel launch failure then container crash.

anya.p That means disable paging not enough or didn't take. Did the env toggle get applied? It needs a full restart with ATTENTION_PAGING=0 in the pod spec.

david.r I've scaled down batch workers for the two tenants to limit request concurrency while we stabilize. `kubectl scale deployment/batch-worker --replicas=1 -n tenant-a` and same for tenant-b.

ml-infra I'm attaching the allocator debug dump (snippet):
```
ALLOCATOR SNAP 2026-03-15T02:14:22Z
active_pages=18432
resident_pages=17000
free_fragments=9123
largest_free_run=128
avg_fragment_size=6.2
kv_eviction_rate=0.02
leak_estimate_bytes=+1.9GB last_24h
```

anya.p Leak estimate +1.9GB in last 24h matches slow creep theory. Two mitigation knobs: bump pool_coalesce_threshold and increase eviction aggressiveness. I'll prepare a hotfix to change `kv.pool.coalesce=32` -> `64` and `kv.eviction.target=0.85` -> `0.75`. Needs rollout on Dedicated and Hosted in region.

sre-lead Approve hotfix as emergency. Keep canary to single node then roll. sam.h, apply to prod-kv-09 first as canary.

sam.h Patching prod-kv-09 with new config and restarting runtime now.

oncall-bot Patch applied to prod-kv-09 at 3472005723, canary restart initiated.

(2m later)
ml-infra Canary looks stable: memory plateaued, fragmentation ratio down to 0.45. No OOMs so far. Error rate in US-W dropped to 0.9%.

david.r Good. I'll coordinate rolling to remaining nodes with 1 node at a time, 5m monitoring window.

anya.p Also capturing HK data for heap maps and running `cuda-memcheck` on a replicated node to see if there's a kernel-level issue. If that comes back green, it's allocator-level.

sre-lead Customer impact note: brief 503s for ~3% of requests over a 12m window. No long-term data loss. Outreach: support should notify affected tenants with summary and that we're mitigating.

sam.h Rolling to prod-kv cluster now, starting with prod-kv-10. Will update as nodes finish.

(rolling updates across cluster, 6 nodes, ~1h)

ml-infra Post-roll metrics: fragmentation ratio baseline down to 0.30 cluster-wide, leak estimate trending flat. No further OOMs observed. Latency tail returned to normal.

anya.p Follow-up tasks for postmortem:
- collect full allocator heap dumps from prod-kv-08 pre-restart (we have partial)
- reproduce leak locally with long-context replay harness
- add eviction rate autoscaler trigger when fragmentation > 0.6
- add monitoring alert for gradual leak slope (e.g., >200MB/6h)

sre-lead Assigned postmortem owner: anya.p. ETA draft postmortem EOD tomorrow.

david.r I'll coordinate customer comms with support.

oncall-bot Incident closed (mitigated) at 3472005755. Summary: KV paged-attention allocator fragmentation + slow memory creep -> OOMs + node flaps. Emergency hotfix applied (kv.pool.coalesce and kv.eviction changes) rolled cluster-wide. Impact: transient 5xx ~3% for ~12m in us-west-2. Postmortem assigned.

sam.h thx everyone. leaving notes in #incidents-log and creating follow-up PR for an autoscaler rule. :thumbsup:

anya.p adding bump to test matrix to ensure paging path exercised under high-batch loads.

sre-lead closing thread, will ping for review once postmortem draft ready. :eyes:
